After any manual price edit follow.current goes false and every number on the tab is computed off the typed price while the chip still reads LIVE. Every rule in ladder-rules.json assumes the fixed A=5.82 / B=-17.029 model. Roughly 40 lines of header plus fitEMA and the modelA/modelB prop threaded through five components.

sections.name: Light-mode toggle + injected light CSS
sections.shows: Sun/moon icon that injects ~110 lines of CSS remapping dark colors to light.
sections.source: Hardcoded style block, matched against inline styles by attribute substring.
sections.reason: The largest single block in the shell, and the most brittle thing in the file: every rule matches on a serialized inline-style substring like [style*="background: rgb(7, 15, 31)"], so it breaks silently the moment any hex in 2,887 lines changes. Its neighbor block (mobile) has already rotted the same way. A dark terminal dashboard does not need a second palette.

sections.name: Mobile style injector
sections.shows: Nothing visible; rewrites grids and font sizes below 700px.
sections.source: Hardcoded CSS string, applied by MutationObserver + resize + load.
sections.reason: He uses this on a phone daily and part of it no longer matches the JSX. Fix the stat-card selector and delete the three rules that target elements which no longer exist.

The band-dial rules at 2864-2866 target a 68px circle that no longer exists.

defects.where: index.html:2453-2459 (chip) with follow ref at 2204 and 2540
defects.what: The header chip reports fetch status, not display status. Any keystroke in the price box sets follow.current=false, after which the poller keeps setting liveFetch to "live" while priceStr stays at whatever he typed. Chip reads "● LIVE PRICE" while the quantile, the band, the ticker, the vs-FV card, the rail needle and the chart dot are all computed off a stale manual number. This is the most likely source of "I don't even know if it works properly."

No alert or notification path exists anywhere in index.html. The comment {/* Alert bell + theme toggle */} promises a bell that was never built. Pushes come only from a separate private repo (btc-monitor) on a GitHub Actions cron restricted to 13:00-21:59 UTC on weekdays, and nothing on this page shows the monitor's last run, so a failed or throttled cron is completely invisible here. That is why he gets no pings, and the site currently cannot tell him.

Two different quantiles are rendered within 200px of each other under near-identical labels. The stat card's value is q, computed from the typed/live price; its background and border color come from tier, which is derived from qM, the monthly close. On any day the live price has crossed a band line, the card shows one clock's number in the other clock's colors.

The mobile stylesheet collapses a stat grid matching [style*="repeat(4, 1fr)"], but the stat grid is repeat(3,1fr). Three cards with 22px values stay three-across on a phone. He reads this site on a phone daily.

Duplicate opacity prop on the band <path>: opacity={b.dim ? 0.35 : 0.9} is immediately overridden by opacity={0.7}. The dim flag on the 99.9 and 95 bands is dead, so all six band lines render at equal weight and the four lines that actually define the ladder do not stand out. Also emits a React duplicate-prop warning.

fetchHistory has no fallback. fetchPrice falls back from CoinGecko to Coinbase, but the 365-day history call does not. A CoinGecko 429 (routine on the free tier from a browser origin) leaves liveHistory null, which kills monthlyClose() and silently drops the band read to the live price — degrading the site's primary function with only one line of small grey text saying so.

The chart's price line double-sources the last 12 months. Every BTC_HISTORY seed point is pushed unconditionally, then live dailies are bucketed weekly and pushed as well; the 5-day dedupe keeps whichever sorts first. Seed values for the recent months are hand-rounded (105000, 85000, 67250) and can suppress the real prints, so the most-looked-at segment of the line is the least accurate.

bandRows, bandsAbove, bandsBelow, nearestAboveQ and nearestBelowQ are computed on every render of BTCPowerLaw and never read. Grep confirms one occurrence each for nearestAboveQ and nearestBelowQ. Leftover from a removed nearest-band highlight.

The entry doc describes a site that no longer exists: three tabs named Ladder / Signals / EO Tracker, a collector/ pipeline, signals.html, and optional ntfy alerts configured in config/manual.json. The live tabs are Ladder / MSTX / Playbook and Signals was retired in August. Anyone opening the repo cold, including a future agent, is told the wrong alert mechanism.
isThirdFriday is defined and never called (one grep occurrence). nextOpex does not use it.
const displayName = (name) => name — an identity wrapper with a single call site at 2599.

Dead mobile selectors. [style*="repeat(5, 1fr)"] matches nothing (the only repeat(5 in the JSX is repeat(5,minmax(66px,1fr)) at 2158). The three width:68px/height:68px band-dial rules target a circular dial that no longer exists; 68px now only appears as a grid column width at 2129.
Footer build stamp "build Sep 17 2026" is a hardcoded string and index.html was last modified Sep 18. It will be wrong after every edit.
Price presets run 75K to 250K in 25K steps. The seed's last spot is 67,250, so every preset is above the market and none is reachable from where BTC is.

TODAY_DAYS is evaluated once at module load and used to cap the upper bands' time decay in bandOffset. The poller rolls `today` so the page survives midnight, but the decay cap does not roll with it — a tab left open for weeks keeps stale upper-band offsets.

minimal_layout: Header: title, tab bar, and one status line that says what is driving the numbers (live price and its age, or MANUAL) plus the monitor's last run

The read: band name and ticker, the quantile, and one subline for fair value and vs-FV — the merged stat cards and tier card, keeping the 4-segment rail, the needle, the rotate-up/rotate-down prices, and the monthly-close vs live-touch sentence
Structure: the long 0.75-delta strike at +12 months and the short band-ceiling strike at +90 days, with its BTC price
The rules, trimmed to gate, entry, size and exit — with the gate rendered as live state (BTC daily close vs its 50-day) rather than prose
Power law chart: history line plus the four ladder bands and their fills, today marker, price dot, lookup marker
Price lookup: date picker with opex steppers, the six band prices at that date, the actual print when past, and today's quantile carried forward — with the single BTC/MSTR unit toggle living here
summary: The Ladder tab says the same thing four times and then asks him to pick a model. The quantile appears in a stat card, on the rail needle, and in the tier card's sentence; the band and structure rules appear as live numbers in the tier and Structure cards and again as prose in the rules card and again in the footer; the Forward Price Projections table's 66 cells are entirely subsumed by the Price Lookup directly beneath it. Cutting Forward Table, the band-history card, the preset row, the EMA model selector, the light-mode layer and the footer takes roughly 300 lines out of the shell without losing a single thing he acts on. Two defects explain his other two complaints. \"I don't know if it works\": the header chip reports whether the fetch succeeded, not whether the page is showing that fetch, so it reads LIVE while every number on the tab is computed off a price he typed — and a few inches below, the quantile card prints the live-price quantile in the monthly-close band's colors. \"I don't get any pings\": there is no alert code in index.html at all. The comment above the theme toggle still says \"Alert bell + theme toggle\" for a bell that was never built; pushes come only from the separate private btc-monitor repo on a weekday-only GitHub Actions cron, and nothing on this page reports whether it ran. Also real and worth fixing while in there: the mobile stylesheet collapses a four-column stat grid that is now three columns, so the top of the page never collapses on his phone; the chart's six band lines all render at the same weight because a duplicate opacity prop overrides the dim flag; the 365-day history fetch has no fallback, so a routine CoinGecko 429 silently disables the monthly-close band read that is the site's primary output; and README.md still documents a Ladder/Signals/EO-Tracker site with ntfy alerts that has not existed since August.
